{{MEinfobox
|name=Tremor
|cg=Tremor.png}}
{{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} is a Status Effect that will raise the Stagger Threshold of an afflicted unit equal to the {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Potency on {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}. Tremor Count decreases by 1 at turn end, and may be decreased by Skills that trigger {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}.

{{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} is linked to the {{Icons|Sloth}}Sloth Sin Affinity.

==Strengths & Weaknesses==
{{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} is a Status Effect that deals damage to Stagger Thresholds rather than HP damage. While this is effective on enemies that have multiple Stagger Thresholds, it is nearly useless against other enemies. The basis of a Tremor team is to make use of the fact that Staggered enemies take +50% damage for every level of Stagger they suffer, but {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}}'s general difficulty dealing damage makes it less powerful than fixed damage Status Effects. To resolve this issue, Fusion Tremor gifts <u>create additional Stagger Thresholds</u>, allowing Tremor teams to deal high damage in [[Mirror Dungeons]].


{{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} is most effective against enemies that have many Stagger Thresholds and low HP. Tremor Identities usually have a {{Icons|Sloth}} Sloth or {{Icons|Gloom}} Gloom skill, and {{Icons|blunt}}Blunt attacks are the most common.

{{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} has a lot of downsides, but is particularly weak against enemies with a low number of Stagger Thresholds and high HP, such as [[Refraction Railway]] Encounters or Main Story Boss fights. Because damage to a Stagger Threshold does not count as HP damage, high Tremor Potency does not by itself convert to damage, and can often be useless: once an enemy recovers from Stagger, causing a {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}} will do nothing if there are no remaining Stagger Thresholds. Compared to other Status Effects, {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} deals the least damage and suffers from the most complications. To circumvent this, {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Conversion|r}} and {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Entanglement|r}} were added to the game, creating different versions of Tremor with bonus effects.


Teams focusing on base {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} primarily focus on Staggering enemies and then dealing damage while they are Staggered. The limitations of this strategy is that most Identities that inflict Tremor are not particularly high damage dealers, meaning that the total damage dealt is lower than teams that use fixed damage Status Effects like {{StatusEffect|Rupture|x}}[[Rupture]] or buffs that enable high damage like {{StatusEffect|Charge|x}}[[Charge]].

==Self-Tremor==
Some Identities gain {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} when using their skills, and use Tremor Count as if it was {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}} to improve the effectiveness of their skills. Tremor used in this way still functions as a debuff, meaning that fighting enemies that inflict {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} can either be dangerous or a quick and convenient way to allow a self-Tremor Identity to function at maximum capacity. Unlike {{StatusEffect|Charge|b}}, Identities with self-Tremor can save up to 99 {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Count, which can be very powerful in long fights.

==Amplitude Conversion, Amplitude Entanglement, & Superposition==
There are two methods of converting between Tremor types, but both versions convert from normal {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} into a different version (marked by a different color) without changing Potency or Count values. {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Conversion|r}} converts the current Tremor type into the newly applied one. {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Entanglement|r}} superimposes multiple varieties of Tremor at the same time, but all varieties of special Tremor will expire at the end of the turn. After {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Entanglement|r}} has been inflicted, superimposed Tremors will display as the Status Effect {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Superposition|d}}. Inflicting {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Conversion|r}} or {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Entanglement|r}} on a unit with {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Superposition|d}} will continue to add different varieties of Tremor, so it is theoretically possible to inflict all versions of Tremor at the same time.

==Unique Tremor: Explanation & Strategy==
<span class="mw-customtoggle-TremorTypes" style="float:left">[<font color="#b88d00">Show/Hide</font>]</span><br>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" id="mw-customcollapsible-TremorTypes">
{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Decay|d}} inflicts 1 {{StatusEffect|Defense Level Down|d}} for every 4 Tremor Potency. If an enemy is at 99 {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Potency, they will suffer 24 {{StatusEffect|Defense Level Down|d}}, which equates to about 50% more damage taken from attacks. The specifics depend on the difference between an attacker's Offense Level & the enemy's defense level, but {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Decay|d}} can allow all attacks to deal greatly increased damage. Fixed damage from Status Effects will not be increased. The main detriment to this version of Tremor is the requirement for extremely high Tremor Potency to get the highest damage bonus. 


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Fracture|d}} increases the Stagger Level of Staggered opponents by 1 as long as the sum of {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Potency and Count is 20 or higher. Each Stagger Level increases damage taken by 50%, and {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Fracture|d}} has relatively easy conditions to meet, so this effect is extremely powerful against enemies with many Stagger Thresholds. The main detriment to this version of Tremor is that it behaves like completely normal Tremor until the enemy is Staggered. If you are fighting enemies that do not have many Stagger Thresholds, the damage output will be low, especially compared to the always-present damage bonus of {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Decay|d}} or {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}}.


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}} deals {{Icons|Sloth}}Sloth damage equal to Tremor Potency on {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}. This effect is extremely powerful because it resolves the fundamental downside of {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}}: being unable to deal damage. {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}} damage ignores damage reduction from buffs (like {{StatusEffect|Protection|b}}) and level scaling, but does not ignore enemy resistances / weaknesses to {{Icons|Sloth}}Sloth. A Tremor - Reverb team is focused around Bursting Tremor frequently while also preventing a Tremor stack from expiring. Because of the requirement for high Tremor Count, the E.G.O [[Everlasting Faust]] and [[Effervescent Corrosion Rodion]] are very useful. {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Entanglement|r}} is generally not recommended because it will remove {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}}, but can be extremely powerful if entangled with {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Everlasting|d}}. Functions similarly to {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Scorch|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Hemorrhage|d}}.


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Everlasting|d}} gives a set chance for an additional {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}} to trigger on {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}. The bonus chance is 1% per Tremor Potency and 1% per Tremor Count, calculated separately (= up to 2 bonus {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}s), with a cap of 50% chance for both possible bonuses. Under ideal conditions (50+ Tremor Potency & Count), {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Everlasting|d}} will, on average, inflict 1 bonus {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}} for every {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}. <u>These additional Tremor Bursts do not lower Tremor Count</u>. This allows {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Everlasting|d}} to double the effectiveness of Tremor. This effect is extremely powerful when {{StatusEffect|Amplitude Entanglement|r}} Entangled with {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}}. If the E.G.O [[Everlasting Faust]] is used on an enemy with 89+ Potency and 40+ Count of {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}}, the attack will Burst Tremor an average of '''8 times, dealing 792 {{Icons|Sloth}}Sloth Damage''', and allow other attackers to deal on average 198 Sloth damage when triggering {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}} that turn. This allows a Tremor team to have a damage output close to {{StatusEffect|Rupture|x}}[[Rupture]], {{StatusEffect|Bleed|x}}[[Bleed]], or {{StatusEffect|Sinking|x}}[[Sinking]].


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Chain|d}} causes units to gain 1 {{StatusEffect|Clash Power Down|d}} for every 10 {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Potency, with a maximum reduction of 3 {{StatusEffect|Clash Power Down|d}} per turn. This is most effective against bosses with only one or two parts, and is a guaranteed way to make the fight significantly easier. 3 clash power is equivalent to a level difference of 9, or 9 {{StatusEffect|Offense Level Down|d}}, but unlike Offense levels, it has no impact on damage dealt. While this effect is strong, {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Chain|d}} does not cause any form of damage increase, making it useless against enemies you can already win clashes against.


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Distribution|b}} grants up to 5 {{StatusEffect|Offense Level Up|b}} based on the total amount of Tremor Count on all allies. Specifically, the total Tremor Count is divided by the number of allies - in a 7 Sinner battle, this means that 7 Count is needed for 1 Offense Level, 14 Count for 2 Offense Levels, and so on. Usually, multiple self-Tremor Identities are needed to get full value from Distribution, but it's also possible to deploy less Sinners than the maximum in order to decrease the Tremor Count thresholds needed to get each Offense Level. <br>
Currently, the only way for the player to gain Distribution is through the {{GiftTT|Entanglement Override Sequencer|25|t}} E.G.O Gift available from the [[List of Floor Themes/Timekilling Time BokGak|Timekilling Time BokGak Theme Pack]].


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Clockwinding|b}} increases the affected unit's max speed and causes them to inflict +1 Tremor Potency or Count when inflicting Tremor on an enemy, at the cost of 1 Tremor Count on self. This effect is particularly useful for increasing Tremor Count application, but is currently limited to [[Asymmetrical Inertia Heathcliff]] and therefore Heathcliff Identities.


{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Scorch|d}} causes units to take {{Icons|Wrath}} Wrath damage by the sum of {{StatusEffect|Burn|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Potency divided by 2 on {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}. While it functions similarly to {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Reverb|d}}, Scorch requires high Potency of two status effects rather than just one to cause the maximum damage output of 99 fixed Wrath damage per Burst. On a purely Tremor focused team, Scorch can deal a max of 50 Wrath damage per Tremor Burst without any Burn Potency. This can be very useful against enemies resistant to {{Icons|Sloth}} Sloth damage but weak to {{Icons|Wrath}} Wrath. Like other forms of fixed damage, Scorch ignores damage reduction from buffs (like {{StatusEffect|Protection|b}}) and level scaling, but does not ignore enemy resistances / weaknesses to {{Icons|Wrath}}Wrath.

{{StatusEffect|Tremor - Hemorrhage|d}} causes units to take {{Icons|Lust}} Lust damage by the sum of {{StatusEffect|Bleed|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} Potency divided by 2 on {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}. Hemorrhage functions nearly identically to {{StatusEffect|Tremor - Scorch|d}}, requiring Bleed instead of {{StatusEffect|Burn|d}} Potency. Due to the nature of Bleed, higher care may be needed to maintain enough Count for both Bleed and Tremor. Similar to Scorch, Hemorrhage can be useful against enemies resistant to {{Icons|Sloth}} Sloth but weak to {{Icons|Lust}} Lust.</div>

==Identities & E.G.O==
While there are many Identities and E.G.O that inflict both {{StatusEffect|Tremor|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}}, there is also a relatively large pool that only Bursts Tremor. E.G.O Skills frequently trigger {{StatusEffect|Tremor Burst|d}} without reducing Tremor Count.
